title: Team Evaluation
description: Preserves organization-, roster-, unit- and environment-level arguments that can affect multiple current or future players.
principles: A team segment is not merely a list of player mini-takes.
Preserve organization-wide mechanisms and then link affected players.
Keep offense, defense, coaching, personnel, cap and time horizon separate when the source does.
Do not convert broad team context directly into player action recommendations.

dimensions.description: Front-office priorities, competitive window and strategic direction.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the direction and the evidence used to infer it.
detection_questions: What is the organization trying to build or change?
Is the source describing a short rebuild, contention window or uncertainty?

dimensions.description: Head coach, coordinators and staff continuity or change.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain staff roles, responsibilities and source-supported implications.

dimensions.description: Offensive or defensive system and tactical identity.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Explain the system and how it changes role or volume distribution.
detection_questions: What does the team want to do structurally?
Which personnel groups or concepts matter?

dimensions.description: Roster composition, positional competition and depth.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the depth-chart structure and uncertainty, not only starter names.
detection_questions: Where are the clear roles, competitions or weak points?

dimensions.description: Expected pace, play volume, pass/run mix, target concentration or committee use.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep the source mechanism connecting team behavior to fantasy opportunity.
detection_questions: Does the source expect concentration or rotation?

dimensions.description: Cap health, major contracts, flexibility and roster-control constraints.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve how financial structure affects retention, additions, cuts or role security.
detection_questions: Which contracts or cap constraints shape decisions?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain investments and their interpreted organizational signals.
detection_questions: What did draft capital, free agency or trades reveal?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve strengths and how they can support player production.
detection_questions: What does the team do well and why?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve weaknesses, failure paths and affected roles.
detection_questions: What can suppress volume, efficiency or scoring?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Separate current role context from later roster or cap changes.
detection_questions: What changes after this season or contract cycle?

dimensions.description: Players directly affected by the team-level thesis.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Link players and their relation without replacing the independent team take.
detection_questions: Which players gain, lose or face uncertainty because of this team context?

dimensions.description: Open competitions, unknown staff behavior or projection limits.

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Would the team argument remain useful if one current player left the roster?
Are staff, scheme, depth chart, cap and acquisition strategy independently reusable where discussed?
Are affected players linked without fragmenting the entire segment into player-only takes?
Does the article explain how team context changes opportunity and not merely list names?
forbidden_distortions: Do not reduce a team preview to isolated player verdicts.
Do not infer precise player usage from generic team optimism.
Do not present cap or contract implications not stated or safely supported by the source.
Do not hide a structural team thesis inside one current player's take.
extension_signals: A recurring team-building concept lacks a dimension.
A new unit or organizational subject type is needed.
The source repeatedly uses cap, ownership or front-office behavior in a new way.
A team episode needs a new article or segment pattern.
